text:
incident-bot: ALERT: prod-usw2 streaming queue depth > 90% of capacity, 95th latency > 800ms, error-rate up 3x. Pager routed to oncall.

alice_oncall: seeing the alert, looking at top-of-queue and active workers. assigning SRE.

ben_sre: joining. initial check: GPU pods saturated, long pending conn count on proxy, backpressure not draining. Likely cascading prefix-cache pressure.

lee_eng: any active rollouts? I didn't push anything recent.

ben_sre: no recent rollout. tail logs show many long-lived streaming connections holding KV caches:
```
proxy: connection_id=12234 hold=45s pending_tokens=800
runtime: kv_cache_hits=low cache_evicts=spike
```

ciara_ops: customers on dedicated pools unaffected, this is hosting prod-usw2 only. traffic spike from a partner integration + some low-TTL prefixes.

alice_oncall: we need a mitigation that buys time and reduces per-connection pressure. proposal: temporarily pause server-push streaming responses for the region and flip to short-polling / non-streaming responses for API route /v1/chat/stream. Thoughts? cc @rachel_product for user-impact.

rachel_product: we should avoid breaking behavior if possible. But if we can return equivalent final payloads (non-chunked) and add retry guidance in the response headers, customers should be OK for a 20-60m window. need comms plan.

mario_support: prepping a short status note we can post to status.redwood: "We are temporarily switching streaming responses to non-streaming to improve latency. No data loss expected; some clients may experience longer TTFB."

ben_sre: plan: 1) flip feature flag for region-prod-usw2 to disable streaming push 2) roll proxy rate-limit policy to shape bursts 3) watch latencies and queue depth. I'll run the toggle now and post output.

ben_sre: running: `POST /ops/feature-toggle {"region":"usw2","streaming_push":false}`

ben_sre: response: `{ "status": "ok", "activated_by": "ben_sre", "change_id": "chg_20260317_01" }` :white_check_mark:

ciara_ops: applied proxy shaper: `rate-limit: 150rps per-api-key; burst 250 for 30s`

alice_oncall: confirm clients will get `X-Redwood-Stream: disabled` header and the same final output in a single response?

lee_eng: yes — runtime will buffer final tokens up to 16k tokens then return final JSON. SDKs will see no schema change; streaming hooks will see connection closed sooner. We should add a short deprecation warning in the headers for the window.

rachel_product: approved user message. @mario_support can you publish and coordinate with comms_bot for in-app banner?

mario_support: posting now. status page updated. in-app banner draft: "Temporarily switched streaming to non-streaming in US-WEST-2 to stabilize latency. We expect normal streaming to resume within 1 hour."

comms_bot: banner posted to prod-usw2, incident-tracking updated: https://status.redwood/incident/chg_20260317_01

ben_sre: monitoring: 95th latency dropped from 820ms -> 210ms within 90s, queue depth dropping. error-rate returning to baseline.

alice_oncall: good. tracking window 60 min. if stable for 15m, start rolling back proxy shaper. if stable for 45m, plan to re-enable streaming.

lee_eng: note for SDK teams: we will emit `X-Redwood-Stream-Restored: true` when we flip back. please avoid aggressive reconnects.

mario_support: flagged a few enterprise customers who use streaming heavily and emailed them directly. no escalations so far.

ben_sre: keep monitoring. logs look healthy. I'll hand off to night oncall in 30m with runbook steps.

alice_oncall: handing off to @night_oncall and leaving notes: mitigation active, changelog chg_20260317_01, revert command `POST /ops/feature-toggle {"region":"usw2","streaming_push":true}`.

night_oncall: acked. I'll watch the metrics and coordinate rollback when safe. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in place, streaming push paused in prod-usw2, status page updated.
